description: Labor rates by geography x role. Two KINDS of labor are held here and must never be interchanged: PROCESS labor (the people doing the work being assessed) and IMPLEMENTATION labor (the engineers building the AI solution). Figures are MARKET COMPENSATION, not fully-loaded employer cost — the employer load is applied separately and is currently unresolved.

_meta.no_silent_fallback: If the geography or role has no entry, the lookup returns UNRESOLVED. Never substitute another geography's or role's rate.
_meta.us_process_labor_note: US process labor is NOT duplicated here. It lives in data/sector_benchmarks/*.json (US BLS OEWS wages) where it already carries its citation. Duplicating it would risk drift. This file holds India process labor, plus engineering labor for both geographies.

fully_loaded_multiplier.rationale: None of the sourced figures below are fully-loaded employer cost; they are cash compensation as reported to salary aggregators. A 1.3x-1.6x India ITES/BPO loading (benefits, employer PF/ESI, facilities, overhead) is commonly cited in industry literature, but NO specific citation has been established. Applying it is an explicit assumption and must be shown as one.
fully_loaded_multiplier.source: unsourced — do not present as an industry figure

entries.source: Payscale — Average Customer Service Agent Salary in India
entries.notes: MARKET CASH COMPENSATION (base + bonus + profit sharing), NOT fully-loaded. Entry-level/generalist agent, the role most applicable to high-volume ticket handling.
entries.limitations: Small self-reported sample (n=67) and the underlying page was last refreshed mid-2025. Retrieved directly; the low bound reads 171,000 on the page (an earlier draft of this registry recorded 176,000).

entries.notes: For tier-2/escalation roles requiring product or technical depth. Distinct from the generalist agent entry and NOT interchangeable with it.
entries.limitations: Glassdoor blocks automated retrieval, so this figure was supplied rather than read from the page in this session. City-level medians run higher (Bangalore/Mumbai/Chennai ~6.5-6.8L vs 6.1L national); city refinement is not modelled.

entries.source: ERI SalaryExpert — Accounts Payable Clerk Salary in India
entries.sample_basis: Employer + employee survey methodology (ERI); cross-checked against Indeed and Glassdoor
entries.notes: ERI used as the median because its methodology is more transparent than ML-predicted aggregator figures, and it sits between the Indeed low (348,103) and the Glassdoor high (700,367) rather than at either extreme.
entries.limitations: salaryexpert.com returns HTTP 403 to automated retrieval, so this was not read from the page in this session. The Glassdoor cross-check high is based on n=41, a small sample treated as an upper bound only. The low-to-high spread is unusually wide (2x) and should be treated as genuine uncertainty about the role definition.

entries.notes: IMPLEMENTATION labor — the cost of building and integrating the AI solution, never the cost of the process being automated.
entries.limitations: Glassdoor blocks automated retrieval. The 3x low-to-high spread reflects India's real experience-band range (IT-services vs product-company comp); the national median represents no specific company tier.

entries.source: assumption — no primary source established for a fully-loaded US engineering rate
entries.notes: Retained so US implementation costing works, but it is an assumption and is tagged as one. Stated as an hourly figure already inclusive of load, so the fully-loaded multiplier is NOT applied to it.
entries.limitations: Unsourced. Replace with a real contractor rate card or the organisation's own loaded cost before this appears in a report.
